negative_and_limited_results: The oblique workload had 193/1024 non-bitwise-identical raw distances, with recorded maximum difference 4.440892098500626e-15 mm2. Other four workloads were bitwise identical. The preserved scalar controls and all 15 contact-set/first-witness checks passed on this runtime.

Large-coordinate contact calls took about 60.1-60.8 ms versus a 55.46 ms pooled scalar-distance median; zero-tolerance tangency contact took 51.60 ms versus a 49.54 ms scalar-distance median. These single contact-call observations include fallback and index work and are not paired same-API performance estimates. They show that the raw-distance improvement does not guarantee faster contact decisions.
The includes_near_threshold_scalar_fallback field denotes the enabled code path, not a measured fallback count. Actual fallback counts were not recorded.

Raw distance and contact-index arrays were not retained, only hashes, match counts and maximum differences. This audit verifies receipt/source bindings, saved per-workload consistency, timing arithmetic and the reviewed comparison logic; it does not independently recompute geometry outputs.
The 89,147-byte traced-work excess is identical for 1,024 and 16,384 boxes at batch size 256. This observation excludes pre-existing inputs and does not establish a complete process-memory bound.

scope: Static prototype/reference review plus read-only audit of the owner-executed 76 controls and one root-authorized kernel probe. This reviewer did not execute or repeat tests, kernels, timing probes, patient data or native histories.
static_findings: Face crossings, nonempty intervals, active-coordinate stationary minima and the 1e-15 direction cutoff match the preserved scalar algorithm.
Working arrays are chunk-bounded; full distance output is O(N), contact fragments are retained only when nonempty, and earliest contact follows input row order.
Input validation scans bounded chunks before computation; cancellation raises without returning a partial result, including around final and early-return chunks.
Scalar fallback protects near-threshold decisions, but its proximity guard is explicitly not a formal floating-point error bound.
